reconstructed_theorem_text: Theorem: for every measurable space X, probability measures mu and nu, fixed Gamma : (X -> R) -> (X -> R), fixed admissible : (X -> R) -> Prop, and C,a,b in R, assume C,a,b >= 0, mu <= ofReal(a) times nu, nu <= ofReal(b) times mu, and P(mu,Gamma,admissible,C). Then P(nu,Gamma,admissible,(C a) b). The dominations mean respectively mu(A) <= ofReal(a) nu(A) and nu(A) <= ofReal(b) mu(A) for every measurable A. Ent_m(h) means integral_X h(x) log(h(x)) dm(x) - (integral_X h(x) dm(x)) log(integral_X h(x) dm(x)). Every integral is a real Bochner integral over all X, not an extended-real integral; log(0) = 0. Lean totalizes the Bochner integral by assigning zero when integrability fails. P(m,G,D,c) means: for every f : X -> R, D(f), Integrable(f^2,m), Integrable(f^2 log(f^2),m), Integrable(G(f),m), and G(f) >= 0 m-almost everywhere imply Ent_m(f^2) <= 2 c integral_X G(f)(x) dm(x). G and D are fixed outside the test quantifier. This does not assert that every D-test has the stated integrability or sign. P is vacuous if no test satisfies every antecedent, including if D is empty. There is no implicit topology, smoothness, derivative, or structural condition on G. Thus the hypothesis is the mu-test inequality with constant C, while the conclusion is the nu-test inequality with constant C a b, using the same fixed Gamma and admissible.
objects: X, probability measures mu and nu, fixed Gamma and admissible, nonnegative real C,a,b, and universally quantified real tests f.
domains: X is any measurable space; Gamma : (X -> R) -> (X -> R); admissible : (X -> R) -> Prop. C,a,b are finite real numbers. Measure comparison uses extended-real masses; entropy and energy integrals are real over X.
quantifiers: Universally quantify X, mu, nu, Gamma, admissible, C,a,b. Subject to the assumptions, the target predicate universally quantifies f whose nu-specific analytic premises hold. The source predicate separately quantifies f with mu-specific premises.
assumptions: mu and nu have mass one; C,a,b >= 0; mu(A) <= ofReal(a) nu(A) and nu(A) <= ofReal(b) mu(A) for every measurable A. For every f, admissible(f), mu-integrability of f^2, f^2 log(f^2), and Gamma(f), and mu-almost-everywhere nonnegativity of Gamma(f) imply Ent_mu(f^2) <= 2 C integral_X Gamma(f) dmu.
conclusion: For every f : X -> R, if admissible(f), f^2, f^2 log(f^2), and Gamma(f) are Bochner integrable under nu and Gamma(f) >= 0 nu-almost everywhere, then Ent_nu(f^2) <= 2 ((C a) b) integral_X Gamma(f)(x) dnu(x). The real-integral definition of Ent is expanded in reconstructed_theorem_text.
scopes: The same fixed Gamma and admissible are used on both measures. Source test conditions use mu and target test conditions use nu. Neither predicate asserts integrability or sign for every admissible test, so empty admissible classes or absence of qualifying tests can make it vacuous. No topology, smoothness, or structural condition on Gamma is imposed. Entropy uses real integrals with log(0) = 0.
constant_dependencies: The target constant is exactly (C a) b, depending only on the given source C and given domination bounds a,b, uniformly over all qualifying tests. The factor 2 comes from the predicate.
